assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the-idolmaster:yonai-p@u149-anime#u149-full-series-synthesis and the-idolmaster:yonai-p@u149-anime#yonai-p-monograph, the two canonical transcript-derived V1 artifacts at basis_commit, read in full: the Episode 1-12 and OVA full-series synthesis (transcript turn 45) and the post-series Producer authorship and naming analysis (transcript turn 47), used as reviewed repository analysis of the U149 television anime and OVA. The project's corpus map was read for route and scope only; the Episode 1-9 and OVA deep readings are not curated evidence on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. The monograph's authorship rating and the synthesis's self-described input materials are inputs, not conclusions. No manga continuity, game Producer, other Idolmaster Producer, primary audiovisual source, subtitle track or Japanese voice performance is included, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The U149 television anime Episodes 1-12 and the OVA as one completed arc, at episode granularity: the Episode 1 promise, the Episode 8 and 9 failure-support and outing phase, the Episode 10 shift from carrying the live alone to distributing it, the Episode 11 reassurance correction and invited first-name address, the Episode 12 debut, and the OVA as proof of transmissible care. No within-episode chronology, date or pre-series history is established; the manga continuity and any later material are outside this evidence.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph lists fixed traits (short stature, junior position, untidy apartment, temperament, professional weaknesses, ethical instincts, recurring mistakes) and an arc from believing sincerity and constant presence can compensate for lack of authority to building the conditions through which the girls can stand together; synthesis section 5 names the governing error (self-sacrifice treated as the easiest proof of care) and the corrections (presence as returning and remaining available; honesty over easy reassurance; distributing work in Episode 10). Both are literary characterizations with episode-level placement and no conditional rules, and the synthesis records that his self-sacrifice is acknowledged but not fully resolved, so C is not supported; E would deny a coherent series-long account with a named error and its correction.

An episode-indexed arc: the Episode 1 promise not to disappear, tests through work, separation, failure, Koharu becoming lost and Arisu refusing accompaniment, the Episode 10 shift from carrying the live alone to organizing collective ability, the Episode 11 reassurance correction and invited first-name address, the finale philosophy of capacity transfer, and the OVA reception of Yukimi and Kozue as proof that his care became transmissible. No state gating, default rule or transition conditions exist, so C is not supported; E would ignore the located turning points.

The monograph asserts that he has a fixed voice and recognizable speech rhythm but gives no form, pronoun, address pattern or line; the synthesis quotes no Producer dialogue, and its Japanese quotations belong to the girls and Arisu's mother. Nothing about his register is established; this says nothing about his actual speech.

Established locally: an untidy apartment and nearly empty wallet, spending his own money and losing sleep, the Episode 9 outing (heat safety, rest, play, food, photography) and inclusion in Kaoru's culture of shared meals. These answer bounded canon questions about his private disorder and his conduct on one outing; no ordinary routine, habit or preference pattern is described, so D is not supported.

Arisu receives a three-stage relation (respectful distance under Tachibana-san; tested trust when she rejects his reassurance with 「適当なこと言わないでください」; chosen intimacy when she offers 「ありすでいいです」); Chie receives security without a promise of success, complemented by Tsukasa; Kaoru calls him sensei and notices his tiredness; Haru receives bodily advocacy (he wears her skirt); Koharu and Yukimi receive searching and presence in their own spaces; managers receive poor institutional communication. Variation beyond Arisu is thin, adult-peer relations are barely characterized and no recipient-conditioned rule exists, so C is not supported; E would deny the located Arisu stages and the spread of recipients.

Attributed states: emotionally transparent, excitable, visibly insecure, bad at concealing panic, frightened easily, wanting to tell the girls everything will work out, and an understood final philosophy. These are the analysts' readings of visible conduct with no interior sequence located, so D is not supported; NOT_ASSESSED would ignore explicit attributions.

Located responses: he revises after Arisu rejects his generic reassurance, accommodates Haru's discomfort instead of overriding it, negotiates permission for the rooftop live after the adults reject the proposal, and is described as poor at institutional communication. How he argues, escalates or holds a position is not characterized, so D is not supported.

The synthesis carries much of the series' ethics through his conduct: respecting a boundary before intimacy, learning that reassurance can become dishonesty, making failure survivable without placing institutional consequences on the child, entering the child's world, and the shift from martyrdom to capacity transfer; the monograph credits him with ethical instincts and revised ethics. No scene of deliberation is located, the principles are the analysts' reading of the series' argument, and the finale's concert rescheduling is attributed to the adult production, so C is not supported; E would undervalue the richest dimension of both artifacts.
Neither artifact describes a humor or play repertoire for the Producer; excitability and panic are characterized as insecurity, not comedy. Nothing is established and no inability is inferred.

The synthesis declares complete coverage of Episodes 1-12 and the OVA from the Japanese subtitle and audio tracks, frame archives, scene indices and contact sheets, and the monograph is a post-series reading; Producer claims are placed at episode level across the whole run. Nothing in the set verifies those inputs, no claim is located below episode level, and both artifacts are transcript-derived responses, so C is not supported.

Affirmative limitations: the flaw list (disorganized, financially reckless, poor at institutional communication, frightened easily, presumptuous, reassuring before he knows), Arisu's Episode 11 correction, the initial Episode 10 attempt to carry the project alone, Koharu becoming lost under his supervision with emotional rather than procedural repair, and the synthesis's own limitation that his overwork, spending and disordered private life remain unresolved. These are episode-level and interpretive rather than scene-located countercases, so C is not supported.

Episode numbers give coarse placement for the promise (Episode 1), failure support (Episode 8), the outing (Episode 9), the distributed live (Episode 10), the correction and name change (Episode 11), the debut (Episode 12) and the OVA; no within-episode order, date, pre-series history or default state exists, so D is not supported.

scenario_readiness.note: No Producer line is quoted in either artifact and the asserted fixed voice has no recorded content; CONDITIONAL would certify fluent invention as voice. This bounds the evidence set, not the character's speech.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Any point of the completed Episode 1-12 and OVA arc; no within-episode moment or pre-series state is fixed.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: The Third Entertainment Division girls, Tsukasa, senior idols or company managers; no counterpart outside the anime is supported.

scenario_readiness.note: Both artifacts are retrospective literary readings of a completed arc with no prediction protocol, conditional rule or located scene; the monograph's comparisons to other Idolmaster Producers are authorship judgments, not transfer rules. CONDITIONAL would turn thematic synthesis into character transfer.

An untidy apartment, an empty wallet, lost sleep and one outing are bounded canon facts, not an ordinary-life pattern; CONDITIONAL would generalize three or four asserted facts. NOT_ASSESSED would ignore that they are recorded.

conditions: The dilemma is of an attested kind: protecting a child idol without excluding her, honesty versus easy reassurance, carrying a burden alone versus distributing it, respecting a child's boundary before intimacy, or supporting a child after failure without placing institutional consequences on her.
Chronology is fixed to a phase: before the Episode 10 and Episode 11 corrections he tends to martyrdom and premature reassurance; after them to distributed work and honest uncertainty.
Output is a tendency at the level of the synthesis's stated principles (not knowing, continuing to think, not abandoning), never quoted speech.
Institutional outcomes he does not control, such as the rescheduled finale concert or the chairman's intervention, are not credited to his decision.
scenario_readiness.note: His ethical conduct is the most developed element of both artifacts, with episode-located instances and stated principles, but no deliberation is located and the principles are the analysts' reading of the series' argument. READY would adopt that reading as his procedure; NOT_READY would deny the located ethical conduct.

Neither artifact contains romantic relationship content for the Producer; the evidenced relations are professional guardianship of child idols, and the synthesis treats the suspicion voiced by Risa as the series' acknowledgement of the premise's discomfort, not as a relationship. Nothing is established.

conditions: The setting is the U149 Third Entertainment Division's production work in the television anime or OVA, with the attested girls, Tsukasa, senior idols or company managers.

Behavior is limited to attested classes: returning and remaining available, respecting a child's chosen address, honest uncertainty after Episode 11, making failure survivable, entering the child's own space, bodily advocacy and personal expenditure, martyrdom before Episode 10 and distribution after it, and weak institutional communication.
Output is a behavioral description, not quoted speech, and no production procedure, legal detail or industry fact beyond what the synthesis states is invented.
The subject is the anime incarnation only; the manga Producer, game Producers and other Idolmaster Producers are excluded.
scenario_readiness.note: Production work with the division is the center of both artifacts, with around ten episode-located behaviors; readiness is conditional because location stops at episode level, no speech is attested, the inputs are unverifiable from the set and the synthesis leaves his self-sacrifice unresolved. READY overstates; NOT_READY would deny the evidence's core subject.

known_limits.statement: The monograph asserts a fixed voice and recognizable speech rhythm without recording any form, and the synthesis quotes no Producer line; its Japanese quotations belong to Miria, Arisu, Yukimi, Kozue and Arisu's mother. Only the paraphrased Episode 1 promise that he is not going anywhere is attributed to him.

The synthesis lists among the series' unresolved tensions that the Producer's overwork, personal spending and disordered private life are acknowledged but not fully resolved; his Episode 10 growth concerns distributing work, and the monograph's claim of a completed developmental arc is bounded by that limitation.

The monograph distinguishes YonaiP, the anime Producer, from U149P across adaptations and from game-avatar and other anime Producers; its 8.5 to 9 out of 10 authorship rating and its comparisons with AkabaneP, TakeuchiP, Shiny Colors and Gakuen Idolmaster are comparative literary judgments of how authored he is, not behavioral evidence, and the manga continuity is not evidence here.

The finale's earlier concert is the adult production's compromise, and the synthesis records that the chairman's intervention solves key problems without a durable child-centered structure; institutional outcomes are not to be credited to the Producer's decisions.

Koharu becomes lost under his supervision and the anime offers apology and reunion rather than prevention; the monograph lists disorganization, financial recklessness, poor institutional communication, fear, presumption and premature reassurance as narratively real flaws. Reliability in supervision and administration must not be assumed.

Both artifacts are transcript-derived post-series responses with episode-level placement only: no scene timestamp, subtitle line or frame reference is in the set, the Japanese audio and subtitle inputs the synthesis names cannot be verified from it, the project's E01-E09 and OVA deep readings are not curated evidence on this subject, and the corpus map records that no standalone Episode 10-12 readings were exported. Yūki Yonai's voice performance is outside the set. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
